explanation: When light crosses from one medium into another it changes speed and bends — Snell's law n1*sin(theta1) = n2*sin(theta2) says exactly how much. The product n*sin(theta) is conserved across the boundary, shown in the live readout. Going INTO a denser medium (larger n2, like air to glass) bends the ray TOWARD the normal; going into a thinner one bends it away. Slide the two indices and the incidence angle to see the refracted ray swing, and if n*sin(theta1) exceeds n2 the light can't escape at all (total internal reflection).
bullets: n1*sin(theta1) = n2*sin(theta2): the quantity n*sin(theta) is conserved.
Into a denser medium (bigger n) the ray bends toward the normal.
The index n = c/v tells how much the medium slows light down.
